title: Arakhin 9 - Thirty Days Hath…Which Month?
summary: This class explores the Mishnaic rules for the length of the lunar year and the adjustments made to the calendar to maintain alignment with the lunar cycle. It examines the limits on how many months can be designated as 'full' (30 days) or 'deficient' (29 days) in a given year, and how these adjustments impact the timing of holidays like Rosh Hashanah and Shavuot. The discussion also addresses the authority of the Bet Din to set the calendar versus the need to remain reasonably close to astronomical reality.
questions: Why can't we just have a fixed calendar of 29 and 30-day months alternating perfectly?
Why do the rabbis limit how many 'full' or 'deficient' months can occur in a single year?
How does the calendar account for the fact that a lunar year is shorter than a solar year?
What happens if the Bet Din's calendar calculation differs from when people actually see the new moon?
Why does the timing of the Brit Milah sometimes get pushed off by several days?
